LibraryCatalog.target.cfg.ref: I7, I8, I9: discovery, recovery and mutations at 2 projects, 1 journal row at start, 2 mutations, 1 crash and 1 write stop, with a quiet environment (no other tab, no invalidation without a change, the workspace available).

LibraryCatalog.target-environment.cfg.ref: The same properties while another tab changes a root once and settles one journal row this tab is not replaying: 2 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, no crash, no write stop.

LibraryCatalog.target-workspace.cfg.ref: The same properties while the workspace goes away and returns three times: a replay fails with workspace-unavailable, the row is failed until the return re-arms it, and a row that failed on its third attempt stays failed. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, no crash, no write stop. It drops target's second mutation, which takes the configuration to about 80 s.

LibraryCatalog.liveness.cfg.ref: RowEventuallySettled under LiveSpec (weak fairness of the replay and of discovery; the person, a crash and the workspace are not fair), no SYMMETRY: 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 crash, the workspace away once.

LibraryCatalog.today-ref-epoch.cfg.ref: Inventory L5: getProjectListing compares discoveryEpochRef after the pass settles and the listing lands in the query cache later; a pass started by a poll in between moves the epoch without cancelling the query, so a listing of the previous epoch replaces the catalog. Every invalidation after a storage change cancels the query, so the listing that lands still matches storage. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 poll.

LibraryCatalog.today-ref-epoch-safe.cfg.ref: Companion of today-ref-epoch at its bounds: under CatalogFence = ref every other property holds, CatalogReflectsStorage among them, so the window today-ref-epoch reports breaks the epoch rule and not the catalog's contents.

LibraryCatalog.target-access.cfg.ref: I4, I18, AccessAnswerFenced and AccessMatchedById: 2 questions about 2 projects, each resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel whose earlier replies complete late, 1 invalidation with no change, and 1 mutation whose row starts recovering while a question reads; no row at start, no write stop. It drops the crash, which target-access-crash checks with one question; with both questions and the crash the configuration takes about 140 s.

LibraryCatalog.target-access-crash.cfg.ref: The same properties with a crash: 1 question about 2 projects resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel, 1 invalidation, 1 mutation and 1 crash, which loses the open question while its replies are still in flight; no row at start, no write stop.

LibraryCatalog.today-access-loop.cfg.ref: Inventory L8: getProjectRouteAccess (use-project-manager.tsx at 7918b118, lines 2440 to 2572) re-checks the epoch after every read but the recovery set only on the found path; a creation of the asked project journaled while the configuration read is pending moves no epoch, and the loop answers missing while the tab holds a recovering row for the project. 2 questions about 2 projects resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel, 1 invalidation, 1 mutation and 1 crash; no row at start.

LibraryCatalog.access-match-by-id.cfg.ref: I18 rules matching by id and generation: with a reply matched by question id alone, a question asked again about another project is answered from a read of the first project (p2 answered ready from a read of p1). 1 question resting on 1 read, 1 re-ask, 2 projects, no row at start.

LibraryCatalog.env-double-replay.cfg.ref: Another tab settles one row this tab is replaying (OQ6, no lock): every property holds for this tab, which settles its own replay and accounts for the row. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, no crash, no write stop.

LibraryCatalog.env-double-replay-witness.ref: The inherited risk beside env-double-replay, at its bounds: another tab settles a row while this tab replays it, so two tabs replay one row.

LibraryCatalog.no-epoch.cfg.ref: D10 rules the epoch fence: without it a pass that an invalidation overtook (a mutation settling during the scan) replaces the catalog with what storage held before. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation.

LibraryCatalog.export.cfg.ref: The target, labelled, at 1 project, 1 row at start, 1 mutation and 1 access question resting on 1 read, with no crash, no write stop, no workspace loss, MaxAsks = 0 and MaxBumps = 0, so the graph stays under 1 MB (graphs.LibraryCatalog) and the suite has no AccessCancelled, AccessStaleReply or EpochBumped step; I18 generation matching is checked by the model configurations and machine tests, not by suite replay; adding the write stop alone takes it to 47,362 states.

LibraryCatalog.wide.cfg.ref: Narrowed. The formal plan's wide bounds are 3 projects, 3 mutations, 2 crashes, 2 environment steps and 2 access questions; this configuration checks every property at 3 projects, 1 row at start, 2 mutations, 1 crash and 1 write stop, with a quiet environment (2,531,500 states, about 90 s). Adding one environment step to it, a journal row another tab writes or a root another tab changes, exhausts the runner's 1 GB heap.

LibraryCatalog.target-unheard.cfg.ref: Fast-path FW2, index-contract review A1 and A6: one storage change no evidence reports to the discovery index, with 1 mutation and 1 crash at 2 projects and 1 row at start. CatalogWithinStale, NoReclaimWhileCopy and NoStaleReconcile hold with every other property.

LibraryCatalog.target-unheard-workspace..ref: FW2: one change no evidence reports, possibly made while the workspace is away (the offline edit), and the workspace leaving and returning once: the return reads the folder again, so the edit is listed. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, no crash.

LibraryCatalog.target-unheard-access.cfg.ref: FW2: one change no evidence reports and one route question resting on 2 reads: a first read that contradicts the index feeds it and owes a pass (ContradictionIsEvidence), with every other property. 2 projects, no row at start, 1 mutation, no crash. Added beside the review's table so ContradictionIsEvidence is checked in a passing configuration that asks a question.

LibraryCatalog.index-decides-absence.cfg.ref: Index-contract review F1, A1: with AbsenceProof = index, the orphan sweep drops the device state of an id whose directory another client created and the index has not heard of. verifyAbsent, which reads storage, is what keeps NoReclaimWhileCopy. 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 heard change and 1 unheard change: the directory goes, heard, and comes back, unheard.

LibraryCatalog.verify-does-not-feed.cfg.ref: Index-contract review F7, A2(i): a route read that finds storage and the index disagreeing and does not feed the index reads again against the same entry. 1 question resting on 1 read, 1 unheard change, no mutation.

LibraryCatalog.unheard-liveness.cfg.ref: FW2, A4: CatalogEventuallyCurrent under IndexLiveSpec (weak fairness of the audit, the replay and discovery; evidence, the person and the environment are not fair), no SYMMETRY: 2 projects, 1 row at start, 1 mutation, 1 unheard change. Quiescence: CatalogQuiescent.

LibraryCatalog.unheard-no-audit.cfg.ref: Index-contract review F3, A4: with the audit off, nothing this tab does reads a change no evidence reported, so the catalog never lists it; the audit is load-bearing. It replaces the blueprint's earlier unheard-no-evidence limit. unheard-liveness's bounds.

LibraryCatalog.cancel-holds.cfg.ref: FW3 sole-copy cancel: with CancelHolds a delete the authority cancelled (no other copy holds the id, or none could be read) is held failed, as a terminal failure is, so a route question about the whole project is answered recovery-failed. The target clears the row instead. 1 question about 2 projects resting on 2 reads, 1 re-ask or cancel, 1 invalidation, 1 delete mutation; no row at start, no crash.
